---
title: "Data Layout"
---

## Binning Axes

The binning is defined over:

- `m(3\pi)` bins,
- `t'` bins.

A single analysis item is identified by a pair:

`(m(3\pi) bin, t' bin)`.

## Paper-Derived Baseline

From the COMPASS reference publication:

- `m(3π)` range: `0.5 < m(3π) < 2.5 GeV/c^2` in `100` bins,
- `t'` range: `0.1 < t' < 1.0 (GeV/c)^2` in `11` bins.

These numbers are the default context for this presentation and can be adjusted if your Parfait analysis uses a modified binning scheme.

The HEPData release for the resonance-model fit provides data exactly on this `(m(3π), t')` grid, including:

- normalized transition amplitudes for 14 selected waves across all `1100` cells,
- covariance matrices (per cell),
- decay phase-space volumes `I_aa` versus `m(3π)`.

## Conceptual Structure

```text
Dataset
└── m(3π) bin i
    ├── t' bin 1
    ├── t' bin 2
    └── ...
└── m(3π) bin i+1
    ├── t' bin 1
    └── ...
```

## What This Enables

- compare behavior across `t'` at fixed `m(3\pi)`,
- compare behavior across `m(3\pi)` at fixed `t'`,
- study normalization strategy per bin and globally.

Integral definitions used in data-model comparison will be linked in this page once provided from external sources.
